benchmark: shlyokavitsa restoration, exact match by phrase length
why_this_metric: The whole phrase has to be character-perfect. Character error rate is reported alongside it because it is the number that shows how near the misses are.

protocol.pairs: glassbox/shlyokavitsa-pairs, test split — built from Bulgarian Wikipedia, article-disjoint, never seen in training
protocol.decoding: greedy; constrained (wide) is the default and the row to beat

in_corpus_comparison.note: 0.92 on pairs from the model's own training distribution against 0.720 here, constrained. The drop is the finding: Wikipedia is dense with proper nouns and abbreviations, which is where the romanization's irrecoverable collisions live.

reading: n = 200 per length. Constrained decoding costs zero parameters and buys +0.155 exact match at 25 words with an 8.5x lower CER. It works by making structural errors — lost alignment, dropped or duplicated characters — unrepresentable, which is why the gain tracks the structural row and not the ambiguity row. The 0.040 residue at 25 words is the shipped policy accepting spellings people actually type: a legal reading of the input that is not the reference's. It does nothing for the a/u ambiguity, which is information the keyboard destroyed.
measured_on: CPU/MPS reference numerics over frozen weights, greedy, 2026-08-01
device_note: Greedy decoding over frozen weights — deterministic given the same pairs.
tolerance: greedy decoding makes this exact — a differing number means different pairs, not different hardware

superseded.why: n = 40 is too thin to read length-by-length: it puts 10 words above 5, which n = 200 shows is sampling noise. It reproduces exactly at n = 40 and is kept only as provenance.
